coordinates.note: No official LSC page fetched in this session states a numeric coordinate; this is an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim node specifically tagged as the laboratory itself. Per A17, a geocoder source limits kind to campus/approximate rather than underground_lab. Cross-checked 2026-09-17 against the ROR v2 organization record for Canfranc Underground Laboratory (ror.org/02zcam055, also rank 8: geocoder): lat 42.71628, lon -0.52563, about 830 m from this OSM node. Both are institutional geocodes, not surveyed points, and the existing OSM node (tagged specifically to the laboratory building rather than a generic registered address) is kept as the primary value; the ROR point is recorded as a second source for corroboration/future reconciliation.
coordinates.quote: "name": "Laboratorio Subterraneo de Canfranc", lat 42.7493154, lon -0.5162702, Paseo de los Ayerbe, Canfranc-Estacion, Huesca, Aragon, Spain

depth.quote: It has a depth of 800 m under Mount Tobazo.

summary.plain: An underground physics laboratory under Mount Tobazo in the Spanish Pyrenees, reached via a former railway tunnel near the village of Canfranc.
summary.technical: Underground hall beneath Mount Tobazo, Canfranc-Estacion, Huesca, at ~800 m depth, excavated from the disused Somport (Canfranc) railway tunnel near the France-Spain border.
